clue.text: Obvious profit share

parts.note: to clear a sum is to make it as profit
a cut is a share of the takings

explanation.surface: A plain matter of how the profits are divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is plainly defined and unambiguous, a synonym for obvious.

clue.text: Requirement for cowboy's uplifting short story about song?

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
about says the shortened story wraps round the song
short says the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A cowboy needs a heartening little tale about a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns the whole assembly, not one piece: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, so TAIRAL becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is the lasso rope a cowboy uses, so it is a piece of his essential kit.

clue.text: Makes assertions about leaving speleologists

indicators.note: leaving says the abbreviation for about departs from the word for cave explorers

parts.note: speleologists explore caves, so they are cavers
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth on why cave explorers are quitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, so avers means states or asserts.

clue.text: Guard exercising caution around head of state and daughter

indicators.note: exercising suggests the letters of caution being worked over into a new order
around here adds to the sense of things being moved about, so caution, the head of state and daughter are stirred together
head of picks the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A security guard being careful around a head of state and his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' and 'around' together say that CAUTION, S and D are worked over into a new order as one pool of nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper or protector, so a guard in the general sense.

clue.text: Military vehicle's most popular gear?

parts.note: a tank is an armoured military vehicle
the top choice is the most popular

explanation.surface: Asks which kit is the best-loved item for an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover, an item of clothing or gear.

clue.text: Dancing permitted by graduate student?

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Asks whether a graduate student is allowed to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a theatrical form of dancing, so the noun dancing covers it.

clue.text: Jolts minister, possibly in public transport

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a minister is possibly an MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A government minister gets jostled while riding the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumps are knocks or jolts, as on a rough ride.

clue.text: Peers in support of country letters of property

indicators.note: in a down clue, being in support of means sitting underneath, so this piece comes below the other

parts.note: land is a country
lords are peers of the realm

explanation.surface: Lords backing the nation's literature on property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is not alphabet letters but people who let out property.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords are people who let out houses or flats they own.

clue.text: Treatments making ophthalmologist work shifts, initially

parts.note: an ophthalmologist is an eye doctor, eye Dr
OP is the abbreviation of opus, a work

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of shifts

explanation.surface: Medical treatments forcing an eye specialist to work shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyedrops are liquid medicines dripped into the eye, a form of treatment.

clue.text: Short introduction to short shorts (in the USA)

parts.note: brief means short

indicators.note: introduction to takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A brief note on short trousers as Americans call them.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans call men's underpants shorts, as in boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are close-fitting underpants, which in American usage are called shorts.

clue.text: Votes against taking on colliery candidates

indicators.note: taking on says the votes take in, or contain, the pit

parts.note: noes are votes against
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: The ballot goes against the mine's preferred candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominees are people put forward for election or an award, that is candidates.

clue.text: Official document showing father's recreation?

parts.note: pa is father, so father's is pa's
sport is recreation

explanation.surface: A document showing what Dad does for fun?
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official travel document issued by a government.

clue.text: Unfortunately rejected Rodney's case for pay

indicators.note: rejected says the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: case takes the outer letters of Rodney, his casing

explanation.surface: Rodney's pay claim was sadly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALAS into SALA; Rodney's case is R and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed regular pay for work.

clue.text: Omit to fix, and fumble for something the kids might play with

definitions.text: something the kids might play with

parts.note: to skip is to omit
to pin is to fix in place
to grope is to fumble about

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave out a repair and fumble for a children's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is a children's plaything for jumping over as it turns.

clue.text: Animal fat may be soaked

definitions.meaning: animal fats are typically the kind with no double bonds in their chains

explanation.definitionFit: Saturated describes fat with no double bonds, typical of animal fat, and also means drenched.

clue.text: Fellow man mostly being rough at play

indicators.note: at play suggests the letters frolicking into a new arrangement
mostly says being loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man who is rough when playing games.
explanation.walkthrough: BEIN (being without G) plus ROUGH are rearranged by 'at play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbour in the biblical sense is any fellow human being.

clue.text: To have affairs is shrewd — outside sultanate

indicators.note: outside says the shrewd word wraps around the country

parts.note: wise means shrewd
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: Philandering is the clever thing to do once you leave the sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to pursue casual affairs with women.

clue.text: Childminders put on warning mostly for parties with singing

indicators.note: put on says the childminders are attached after the other piece in this across clue
mostly says the warning word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hooter sounds a warning
nannies are childminders

explanation.surface: Nannies get a sort of warning about rowdy sing-along parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Hootenannies are informal gatherings with folk singing.

clue.text: Developing new source of active perfume

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of active

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A new fragrance is being developed from an active ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, emerging or developing.

clue.text: Small party seen in wood only occasionally

indicators.note: seen in says the party sits inside the wood

parts.note: elm is a wood
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A small party is rarely seen in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, happening only now and then.

clue.text: Bush's strange allure

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, turned into another order

explanation.surface: The odd charm of a former US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A laurel is an evergreen shrub, that is a bush.

clue.text: Run through cold in country road

indicators.note: in says the cold letter goes inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Jogging in the cold along a rural lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' looks like jogging, but means pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce with a blade, to run something through.

clue.text: Son chilled outside hotel, getting educated

indicators.note: outside says the chilled word goes round the hotel

parts.note: cooled means chilled
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boy relaxing outside a hotel picks up some learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooled means taught or trained, that is educated.

clue.text: Ejects or throws out leader from medieval tournaments

indicators.note: throws out leader from says the first letter of the tournaments word is removed

parts.note: jousts are medieval tournaments of knights on horseback

explanation.surface: A knight unseats or expels the champion of the tournaments.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to drive out or expel, so ousts means ejects.

clue.text: Steps around first degree of separation

indicators.note: around says the steps go round the first

parts.note: a dance is a series of steps
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Dance steps around a first-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is 1st with the figure 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the amount of space by which things are separated.

clue.text: Working with team's situation in field

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A player working with the team in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Onside is a legal position on the field in football or rugby, behind the ball.

clue.text: Offer for sale held department back somewhat

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A department store keeps some goods back from sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to hawk goods, offering them for sale.

clue.text: Morse, involved in link, gets boring

indicators.note: in says the jumbled name goes inside the link

parts.note: a tie is a link

indicators.note: involved suggests Morse's letters entangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse gets entangled in a connection and finds it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles the name before 'in' tucks it inside. Morse is the fictional Oxford detective of the TV series, which makes the surface feel like a crime story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious or wearisome, so boring.
